mainEntity.name: Do I need dedicated electrical service inside my RV storage building?

acceptedAnswer.text: Adding dedicated 30-amp or 50-amp electrical service is strongly recommended to keep vehicle house batteries charged and run onboard systems safely. Keeping your RV plugged into a shore power receptacle inside the building maintains battery life, runs climate systems during humid or freezing spells, and allows you to prep refrigerators prior to trips. Running a high-draw RV on a standard 15-amp household extension cord risks tripping circuit breakers and damaging sensitive inverter equipment. Planning electrical panel capacity early ensures you have adequate amperage without overloading your home electrical service.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes, installing a dedicated 30-amp or 50-amp outlet protects vehicle electronics, keeps onboard batteries charged, and runs appliances without tripping household breakers.
